In triangle \( ABC \), the angles are \( A = 20^\circ \), \( B = 60^\circ \), and \( C = 100^\circ \). Point \( D \) lies on \( AC \) such that \( \angle BDC = 90^\circ \) and \( CD = 2 \). Find the length of \( AD \).

How many people must be in a room for the probability that at least two people share the same birthday (day and month) to exceed 50%, but also ensuring that there exists a possible arrangement of birthdays (for example, one person could be born on January 1st, and another on January 2nd, but no two people can share a birthday exactly one day apart)?
What is the last digit of the quotient \( \frac{2^{2023} + 3^{2023}}{5} \) ?

A regular 1000-sided polygon is drawn on a unit grid in the complex plane, with vertices at \(1 + i\), \(\omega\), \(i\), and \(-1 + i\) on the complex plane. If \(\omega\) is a root of the equation \(z^{1000} = 1\), what is the area of the union of all triangles formed by any three vertices of the polygon?

Find all polynomials \(P(x)\) with integer coefficients such that, for any positive integer \(n\), the numbers
\[ P(0), P(1), P(2), \ldots, P(n) \]
give pairwise distinct remainders when divided by \(n\).

Let \( S \) be the set of all positive integers \( n \) such that there exists a set of distinct positive integers \( \{a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k\} \) where \( k \geq 3 \) and \( \gcd(a_i, a_j) = 1 \) for all \( i \neq j \), and the polynomial \( P(x) = (x + a_1)(x + a_2) \cdots (x + a_k) - n \) has exactly three distinct integer roots. Find the sum of all elements in \( S \).

Consider a sequence of positive integers \( a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots \) defined recursively by \( a_1 = 1 \) and for \( n \geq 2 \),

\[
a_n = \frac{1}{2} \left( \sqrt{4a_{n-1}^2 + 12n} + a_{n-1} \right).
\]

Find the smallest value of \( n \) for which \( a_n \) is an integer.

Alice, Bob, and Carol play a game using a regular 6-sided die. Alice rolls the die first. If she rolls a 1, 2, 3, or 4, she wins. Otherwise, Bob rolls the die next. If Bob rolls a 1, 2, 3, or 4, he wins. Otherwise, Carol rolls the die last. If Carol rolls a 1, 2, 3, or 4, she wins. Otherwise, the game ends in a draw.

What is the probability that Carol wins the game? Express your answer as a common fraction.

Consider a 2024 x 2024 grid of squares. Alice and Bob take turns coloring squares with Alice going first. On each turn, a player must color a square the same color as an adjacent square (sharing an edge) and may only color a square if it is not already colored. The game ends when no more moves are possible. Let \( N \) be the maximum possible number of squares that can be colored by the two players. Determine the remainder when \( N \) is divided by 1000.

Let \( P(x) \) be a monic polynomial with integer coefficients, such that \( P(0) = 2023 \). If \( P(x) \) has exactly 7 distinct integer roots, find the minimum possible value of \( |P(1)| + |P(-1)| \).

Consider a sequence of positive integers $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ defined recursively by $a_1 = 2$, and for $n \geq 1$,
\[a_{n+1} = a_n + \left\lfloor \sqrt{a_n} \right\rfloor.\]
For how many positive integers $k \leq 2024$ is $k$ equal to $a_m$ for some positive integer $m$?

In the plane, let \( P \) be a regular \( 2023 \)-gon. A non-empty set \( S \) of vertices of \( P \) is called *special* if no three vertices of \( S \) form an equilateral triangle. Let \( n \) be the maximum number of elements that a *special* set can contain. How many *special* sets with \( n \) elements can be chosen from \( P \)?

Note: A *special* set may contain two or three vertices that form an isosceles triangle but not an equilateral one.

Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial of degree 5 with real coefficients, such that $P(1) = 17$, $P(2) = 34$, $P(3) = 51$, $P(4) = 68$, and $P(5) = 85$. Let $r$ be the largest positive real number for which there exists a real number $s$ such that the polynomial $Q(x) = P(x) - rx + s$ has a double root. Find the value of $r$.

Let $P$ be a non-constant polynomial such that for all positive integers $n$, the sum $P(n) + P(n+1) + P(n+2)$ is a perfect square. Prove that there exists a polynomial $Q$ with integer coefficients such that for all positive integers $n$, either $P(n) = Q(n) - Q(n+1)$ or $P(n) = Q(n+1) - Q(n)$.

A circular track with a circumference of 600 feet has two points, P and Q, on it such that the arc between them is 120 feet long. Two runners start at the same time from point P and run at different constant speeds along the track. The first runner runs clockwise and covers 10 feet per second, while the second runner runs counterclockwise and covers 15 feet per second. After how many seconds will they meet for the first time?

In the complex plane, consider the set of points \(P\) such that when \(P\) is rotated by 60 degrees clockwise around the origin, the resulting point \(Q\) satisfies the equation \[|Q-1| = |Q-2| = |Q-3| = |Q-4|.\] Find the distance from the origin to the closest point in this set.

Let S be a set of n points in the plane, with no three points collinear. Show that for any positive integer k, there are at least ⌊(2k - 1)/3⌋ subsets T of S such that any pair of points in T forms an obtuse angle with all other points in S.

A sequence \( \{a_n\} \) is defined as follows: \( a_1 = 1 \) and for \( n \geq 2 \), \( a_n \) is the smallest positive integer greater than \( a_{n-1} \) such that the number of common divisors of \( a_n \) and \( a_{n-1} \) is exactly one. Let \( S \) be the set of all integers from \( 1 \) to \( 1000 \) inclusive. Find the sum of all integers \( k \) in \( S \) such that \( a_k \) is a multiple of \( k \).
How many non-degenerate triangles can be formed where each vertex is a point from a set of 100 points on a 10x10 grid, ensuring that no two vertices are aligned on the same row or column?

Two players alternately paint the faces of a cube blue and green. The first player paints two opposite faces blue and three adjacent faces blue, after which each player paints one face on each turn. If blue is allowed to paint more faces than green, what is the minimum number of additional blue faces a player needs to ensure they have painted more blue faces than green?
Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that $P(0) = 1$, $P(1) = 2$, and for every integer $n$, $P(n)$ divides $P(P(n))$. Find all possible values of $P(2)$.

During a special event, a theater manager decides to sell tickets for three different segments of a show: Segment A, Segment B, and Segment C. The prices of tickets are as follows: $15 for Segment A, $18 for Segment B, and $25 for Segment C. To attract more customers, the manager offers a discount: if a customer buys at least 2 tickets for Segment A, they get a $5 discount on one Segment B ticket. If a customer buys at least 3 Segment C tickets, they receive a free Segment B ticket. On a particular day, 120 Segment A tickets, 90 Segment B tickets, and 60 Segment C tickets were sold. What is the total revenue from these ticket sales, taking into account all discounts?
Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that $P(1) = 17$ and $P(17) = 1$. Find the remainder when $P(2023)$ is divided by $10$.

In a regular hexagon \( ABCDEF \) with side length \( 1 \), points \( G, H, I, J, K, L \) are the midpoints of sides \( AB, BC, CD, DE, EF, \) and \( FA \), respectively. Let \( M \) and \( N \) be the points of intersection of the diagonals \( CE \) and \( AD \), and \( BG \) and \( CF \). What is the length of the line segment \( MN \)?

What is the largest positive integer \( n \) such that there exist positive real numbers \( x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \) satisfying 
\[
\left( 1 + \frac{1}{x_1} \right) \left( 1 + \frac{1}{x_2} \right) \cdots \left( 1 + \frac{1}{x_n} \right) = \frac{5}{2},
\]
\[
\left( 1 - \frac{1}{x_1} \right) \left( 1 - \frac{1}{x_2} \right) \cdots \left( 1 - \frac{1}{x_n} \right) = \frac{2}{5},
\]
\[
x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_n \leq 45,
\]
\[
(x_1 x_2 + x_1 x_3 + \cdots + x_1 x_n + x_2 x_3 + \cdots + x_{n-1} x_n) \leq 150?
\]

Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that $P(0) = 1$ and $P(1) = 2$. If $P(x)$ has a root $r$ that is a rational number and $|r| \leq 1000$, find the maximum possible value of $|r|$ such that $P(x)$ also has an integer root $s$. How many distinct polynomials $P(x)$ exist satisfying these conditions?

Let \( a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n \) be a sequence of positive integers such that \( a_{i+1} = a_i^2 - 2 \) for all \( i \geq 1 \), and \( a_1 = 3 \). Find the smallest \( n \) for which \( a_n \) is divisible by \( 1000 \).

Define a "mountainous function" to be any function $f$ that has at least two strictly increasing intervals of length one each, and then there is a region in which the function is decreasing. For example, $f(x) = x^3$ is mountainous, because $f(1) < f(2) < f(3)$, and then the function is decreasing until $x = 5$.
A function $f$ has at least one "mountain" if there exist real numbers $a,$ $b,$ and $c,$ such that $a \le b \le c$ and $f(a) < f(b) > f(c).$  For example, $f(x) = x^3$ is mountainous, because $f(1) < f(2) > f(3)$, while $g(x) = x^4$ is not mountainous because there are no such numbers $a,$ $b,$ and $c.$  How many mountainous functions of the form $f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$ are there with $a,$ $b,$ $c$ all integers between 1 and 20 inclusive?

Alice and Bob play a game on an infinite grid of unit squares. The game starts with a token at the origin \((0, 0)\). On each turn, Alice can move the token up, down, left, or right by 1 unit, while Bob can rotate the grid \(90^\circ\) clockwise around the origin before Alice moves. The game ends when the token reaches a point \((x, y)\) such that \(|x| + |y| \ge 10\). Bob wins if the game ends on his move, otherwise Alice wins. Which player has a winning strategy?

Let \( f(x) \) be a continuous and differentiable function on the interval \( [0, 1] \) such that \( f(0) = 0 \) and \( f(1) = 1 \). Prove that there exists a point \( c \) in \( (0, 1) \) such that \( f(c) = c \) and \( f''(c) = 2 \).

Let $P(x)$ be a monic polynomial of degree $2023$ with integer coefficients such that $P(1) = 2023$, $P(2) = 4046$, $P(3) = 6069$, and for all integers $n \geq 4$, $P(n)$ is divisible by $1001$. Find the remainder when $P(0)$ is divided by $1001$.

A circular table has 12 evenly spaced points labeled \( P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_{12} \). A bug starts at \( P_1 \). At each step, it can move to either of the two adjacent points with equal probability. After 10 steps, what is the probability that the bug returns to \( P_1 \)?

Lucas is baking cookies. For every 30 cookies he bakes, he saves 30% of the batch. He can sell one cookie every 2 minutes. If Lucas takes exactly 81 minutes to complete 5 batches, then calculate the amount of time (minutes) Lucas took to save a total of 3 cookies during his cookie-baking operation.

On a blackboard, the number  \( 1 \)  is written  $n$  times. At each step, two arbitrary numbers are erased from the blackboard, let them be  $a$  and  $b$ , and then the number  $a+b+ab$  is written on the blackboard. After  $\binom{n}{2}$  steps, there is only one number on the blackboard, let that be  $k$ .
(1) Determine all positive integers  $n$  such that  $n^2-1$  divides  $k$ .
(2) What is the sum of all the possible values of  $k$  when  $n=34$ ?

Find all positive integers \( n \) such that there exists a permutation \( \sigma \) of \( \{1, 2, \ldots, n\} \) for which the sum of the first \( k \) terms \( \sigma(1) + \sigma(2) + \cdots + \sigma(k) \) is not divisible by \( k+1 \) for every \( k \) from \( 1 \) to \( n-1 \).
Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that $f(0) = 1$ and $f(1) = 2023$. Find the smallest possible value of $|f(n)|$ for any integer $n \neq 0, 1$.
Four points $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are placed randomly and independently on a circle of radius 1. What is the expected value of the area of quadrilateral $ABCD$?

In the game of AlphaBetaPrime, two players take turns selecting a positive integer. The first player starts by choosing a number less than 1000 that is not a perfect square. Then, the second player must choose a number greater than the first player's choice that is a perfect square. After that, the first player chooses a number greater than the second player's choice that is not a perfect square, and so on. The game ends when a player cannot make a valid move. The winner is the player who makes the last valid move. If both players play optimally, how many winning positions can the first player force on the board in the first turn?
Find the smallest positive integer n such that the product of all the divisors of n is 10^n.

Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that $P(0) = 1$ and $P(1) = 2$. If $P(x)$ has exactly three distinct integer roots, none of which are divisible by any prime less than or equal to $17$, what is the minimum possible degree of $P(x)$?
What is the remainder when the sum of the first 100 terms of the geometric sequence with the first term 2 and common ratio 3 is divided by 1000?
Let \( f(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( f(0) = 1 \) and \( f(1) = 2023 \). What is the maximum possible number of integer roots of the equation \( f(x) = 0 \)?

Find all positive integers \( n \) for which there exist positive real numbers \( x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \) such that for every \( i = 1, 2, \ldots, n \), the equality \[ \frac{x_i}{x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_{i-1} + x_{i+1} + \cdots + x_n} = \frac{x_i}{x_i^2 + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_{i-1} + x_{i+1} + \cdots + x_n} \] holds.
Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that $P(0) = 1$ and $P(1) = 2$. Prove that there exists a positive integer $n$ for which $P(n)$ is divisible by $2023$.

Given that $a$ and $b$ are integers, find the sum of all possible values of $a + b$ such that the expression
\[x^4 + ax^2 + bx + 2023\]can be expressed as a product of two nonconstant quadratic polynomials with integer coefficients.

Alice, Bob, and Carol play a game using a 3x3 grid and three markers labeled A, B, and C. Initially, the markers are placed at random positions in the grid such that no position is occupied by more than one marker. Each player then takes turns to move their marker to an adjacent square (up, down, left, or right) that is unoccupied. The game ends when a player cannot make a move. The player who cannot make a move loses. Alice moves first, followed by Bob, and then Carol. If each player uses an optimal strategy, who wins the game and what is the sequence of moves that leads to the win?

What is the largest possible number of non-collinear points on a plane with each point having integer coordinates that are no more than 100 units apart from one another, such that the number of distinct distances from each point to its neighboring points is at least its index in the ordered list of the 100 most distant points?

There are two nonempty, finite sets A and B containing only positive integers. Set A has 7 elements and set B has 9 elements. A set C is defined as the set of products of each element in A and each element in B. If set C is a subset of the set of natural numbers, find the smallest possible number of elements in set C.

Alice is playing a game with a $100 \times 100$ grid, where each cell can be colored black or white. Alice starts by coloring the entire grid white. She can make a move in one of two ways:
   1. Pick a row or a column and flip the color of every cell in it (black becomes white, and white becomes black).
   2. Pick a $2 \times 2$ square and flip the colors of its four cells.

What is the minimum number of moves Alice needs to make to ensure that the entire grid is black, if she starts with the entire grid being white?

Let \( P(x) \) be a polynomial of degree 2023 with integer coefficients such that \( P(0) = 1 \) and \( P(n) \) is a perfect square for all integers \( n \). Prove that \( P(x) \) is a perfect square of another polynomial with integer coefficients.

Let $p(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that $p(20) = -101$. For some integer $k$, define the sequence $a_n$ by $a_1 = k$ and $a_{n+1} = p(a_n)$. Determine the minimum possible value of $|k|$, if $a_{20} = -101$.

Let $P(x) = x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d$ be a polynomial with real coefficients such that for some real number $k$,
\[P(k) = P(k+1) = P(k+2) = 0.\]
If $P(2) = 2024$, find the value of $P(0) + P(4)$.

Find the maximum of
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{100} a_i \sqrt{x_i}
\]
over all real numbers \( x_1, \ldots, x_{100} \), where \( a_1, \ldots, a_{100} \) are given positive real numbers.
Given the sequence \(a_n\) defined by \(a_1 = 2020\) and \(a_{n+1} = a_n^{a_n} + 1\), find the remainder when \(a_4\) is divided by 2021.

What is the smallest integer \( k \geq 2024 \) such that there exist positive integers \( a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{2024} \) satisfying
\[
k^2 = \left( a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{2024} \right)^3?
\]

A function \( f \) is defined on the positive integers such that \( f(1) = 3 \), \( f(n+1) = f(n) + 2n + 1 \) for all positive integers \( n \). If \( f(k) \) is a prime number and \( k \) is less than 100, find the sum of all possible values of \( k \).
How many increasing sequences of positive integers $a_1 \le a_2 \le a_3 \le \cdots \le a_{10} \le 2007$ have the same sequence of remainders whether the terms are divided by $3$ or by $5$?

Let $P(x) = x^{2023} + x^{2022} + \ldots + x^2 + x + 1$. A polynomial $Q(x)$ is a factor of $P(x)$ if and only if the roots of $Q(x)$ are $n$th roots of unity for some $n \leq 2023$. Determine the number of distinct monic polynomials $Q(x)$ that divide $P(x)$ and have degree exactly $1011$.
What is the smallest positive integer that can be written as the sum of two positive integers, each of which has at most one odd prime factor, and whose product is a perfect square?

Consider a rectangular grid of size \(m \times n\) where each cell is filled with a distinct integer from \(1\) to \(mn\). We say that two adjacent cells (sharing a common side) have a "balance" if their sum is a perfect square. 

Determine the maximum possible number of balanced pairs of adjacent cells in an \(m \times n\) grid. Assume \(m, n \geq 2\).

In a certain game, a player rolls a fair six-sided die, and each face shows a unique integer from 1 to 6. A move consists of rolling the die and updating a score according to the following rules:
- If the die shows an even number, the player's score is doubled.
- If the die shows an odd number, the player's score is increased by the square of the number shown on the die.
Starting with a score of 1, what is the probability that after five moves, the player's score is exactly 128?

Consider a finite sequence of non-negative integers \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n\) such that their sum is equal to 100. Each integer in the sequence represents the number of fish caught by a different individual in a day. Determine the maximum value of the product \(P = a_1 \cdot a_2 \cdot \ldots \cdot a_n\), given that no individual catches more than 3 fish.

In a \(10 \times 10\) grid, Alice places non-overlapping squares of sizes \(1 \times 1\), \(2 \times 2\), \(3 \times 3\), ..., up to \(10 \times 10\). A square can be placed only if it is entirely within the grid and does not overlap with any other squares. Let \(N\) be the number of possible ways Alice can place these squares without violating the placement rules. Calculate the remainder when \(N\) is divided by \(1000\).

Two sequences $(a_n)$ and $(b_n)$ are defined as follows: $a_0=0$, $b_0=0$, $a_{n+1} = \frac{1}{b_n^2 + 1}$, $b_{n+1} = \frac{1}{a_n + 1}$. Prove that $a_{100} < b_{100} < a_{101}$. 

Let $p_n$ be the number of permutations of the set $\{1,2,...,n\}$ such that for each permutation $\pi$ we have $\pi(i)$ divides $\pi(i+1)$ for all $1 \le i \le n-1$. Determine whether $\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\log p_n}{\log n!}$ exists and find its value if it does.

There are 6 distinct buildings in a city, each with a unique number of floors ranging from 5 to 10. A person starts at the bottom floor of the tallest building and can only move up one floor at a time. Calculate the total number of distinct paths the person can take to reach the top floor of any one of these buildings, assuming each building's floors are sequentially numbered starting from 1.

Two polynomials \( P(x) \) and \( Q(x) \) with integer coefficients satisfy the equation
\[ P(x)^3 - Q(x)^2 = x(x^3 + 2x - 1). \]
Find all possible values for the degree of \( P(x) \).

Let $p(x)$ be a polynomial of degree 2009 with leading coefficient 1 and integer coefficients. Suppose the roots of $p(x)$ are $r_1, r_2, ..., r_{2009}$. Consider a sequence $a_n$ defined as follows: $a_0 = 0$, and for $n \geq 1$, $a_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} r_k \cdot a_{n-k}$, where all $r_k$ are distinct prime numbers. Find the remainder when the smallest positive integer $m$ for which $a_m$ is divisible by $2^{2010}$ is divided by $1000$.

Consider a convex polygon with $n$ sides. Each vertex of the polygon is connected to every other vertex except for those adjacent to it, creating a network of non-crossing diagonals. If the total number of regions formed inside the polygon, including the polygon itself, is $2^n - n - 1$, determine the value of $n$.

Alice and Bob play a game on a coordinate plane, starting from the point (0,0). The game consists of \(n\) turns, where Alice goes first. In each turn, a player moves to a point \((x', y')\) such that \(|x' - x| = a\) and \(|y' - y| = b\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are given positive integers. A player cannot visit a point that has already been visited by either player. If a player cannot move on their turn, they lose. For how many pairs of positive integers \(a\) and \(b\) less than 100 is it possible for Alice to guarantee a win, assuming both players play optimally?
Let \( p(n) \) be the product of the digits of the number \( n \) in base \( 10 \), and let \( s(n) \) be the sum of its digits. For which positive integers \( n \) is \( p(n) + s(n) = n \)?

Find all ordered triples \((x, y, z)\) of real numbers that satisfy the following system of equations:
\[
x + y + z = 6
\]
\[
xy + yz + zx = 9
\]
\[
xyz = 4
\]

Given a function \(f(x)\) defined for all real numbers \(x\) such that \(f(x) = x^4 + 2x^2 + 1\) and a second function \(g(x) = \sqrt{f(x) - 1}\), find the smallest possible value of \(g(x)\) for any real \(x\).

Let \( P(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( P(0) = 1 \) and \( P(1) = 2 \). Suppose further that for any prime number \( p \), the polynomial \( P(x) \) evaluated at \( x = p \) yields a perfect square. Determine the smallest possible degree of the polynomial \( P(x) \).

Let \( f(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( f(0) = 1 \) and \( f(1) = 3 \). Suppose that for every positive integer \( n \), \( f(n) \) is a prime number. Find the sum of all possible values of \( f(2) \).

In a room, there are 12 people with either blue or red eyes, and nobody knows their own eye color. They can see everyone else's eye color but not their own. They can communicate with each other, but they cannot share information about the number of people with each eye color. A rule is in effect: if a person realizes their eye color, they must leave the room immediately without communicating with others. One day, a new person enters the room, tells everyone, "There is at least one person with blue eyes in the room," and then leaves. Assuming everyone is perfectly logical and this is the only information new to them, what is the minimum number of days that must pass before all blue-eyed people have left the room?

There are two unit squares, one in the first quadrant and one in the third quadrant, each with vertices at \((0,0)\), \((0,1)\), \((1,1)\), and \((1,0)\). For each square, a random circle is drawn inside it with a random radius between 0 and 1. If the two circles do not overlap, then draw a line segment between the centers of the two circles. Find the probability that the sum of the lengths of all drawn line segments is at least 2.
In the convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ with vertices $A=(0,1),$ $B=(1,3),$ $C=(4,2),$ and $D=(2,0),$ find the area of the quadrilateral formed by the midpoints of the sides of $ABCD.$
Find all natural numbers $n$ such that $2^n - 1$ divides $10^n - 1$.

We call a natural number \( n \) "balanced" if, when we place \( n \) red balls and \( n \) blue balls in a circle, there exists a point \( P \) such that the number of red and blue balls on either side of \( P \) is equal. For example, the number \( 4 \) is balanced because we can place 4 red balls and 4 blue balls in a circle such that 2 red and 2 blue balls are on either side of point \( P \). Find the number of "balanced" numbers less than 1000.

Let \( P(x) \) be a monic polynomial with integer coefficients. Suppose \( P(1) = 0 \) and \( P(5) = 2023 \). What is the maximum possible number of integer roots of \( P(x) \)?

Suppose \( Q(x) \) is a monic polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( Q(1) = 2023 \) and \( Q(5) = 0 \). What is the maximum possible number of integer roots of \( Q(x) \)?

For a monic polynomial \( R(x) \) with integer coefficients, let \( N(R) \) denote the number of integer roots of \( R(x) \). Given polynomials \( P(x) \) and \( Q(x) \) as defined above, find the maximum value of \( N(P \cdot Q) \).
Find the remainder when the product of the divisors of $2009$ is divided by the number of divisors of $2009$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all real numbers $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$, the determinant
\[\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & x_2 & \ldots & x_n \\ f(x_1) & f(x_2) & \ldots & f(x_n) \\ x_1f(x_1) & x_2f(x_2) & \ldots & x_nf(x_n) \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ x_1^{n-1}f(x_1) & x_2^{n-1}f(x_2) & \ldots & x_n^{n-1}f(x_n) \end{vmatrix}\]
is equal to zero.

What is the maximum possible area of a triangle inscribed in the ellipse defined by the equation $x^2 + 4y^2 = 4$ and one vertex at the point $(1, \sqrt{3}/2)$? Find the maximum possible value for the distance $d$ between the other two vertices, and submit that as your answer. (A vertex of a triangle is a corner point, and there may be more than one vertex at the origin.)

Alice and Bob are playing a game with a magical deck of cards. Each card is labeled with a complex number $z$ such that $|z| = 1$. Alice draws a card and chooses a complex number $a$ such that $|a| = 1$ and she must then calculate $az$. Bob, after seeing Alice's result, draws a card and calculates $bz$ for his chosen complex number $b$ with $|b| = 1$. They repeat this process 10 times. If the product of the 10 results $az \times bz \times \cdots$ equals $-1$, Alice wins. Otherwise, Bob wins. Given that Alice always chooses $a$ such that $|a| = 1$, devise a strategy for Bob to ensure he wins. What is the minimum number of times Bob must choose a specific $b$ to guarantee a win, regardless of Alice's choices?

Suppose you have a set of 12 distinct points in a plane, no three of which are collinear. How many non-overlapping triangles can you form by connecting these points such that no triangle shares any side or vertex with another triangle?

In the coordinate plane, let points A, B, C, and D form a rectangle ABCD with sides parallel to the axes. If the coordinates of point A are (0, 0) and the area of the rectangle is 12 square units, find the number of possible integer coordinates for point D given that the coordinates of both A and C must be integers.

Consider a regular hexagon with side length 1. Let \(P\) be a point chosen uniformly at random inside the hexagon. What is the probability that the distance from \(P\) to the nearest side of the hexagon is less than \(1/2\)?

A circle of radius 1 is inscribed in an isosceles triangle whose two base angles are equal to each other. The circle divides the triangle into regions of the same area. If the area of the triangle is \(A\) and the area of the circle is \(C\), find the ratio \(\frac{A}{C}\).
What is the remainder when the sum of 2015 consecutive positive integers is divided by 1000?

Consider a complex sequence \(\{z_n\}\) defined by \(z_1 = 2 + i\) and \(z_{n+1} = (1 + i)z_n\) for \(n \geq 1\). Let \(P_n\) denote the polygon in the complex plane with vertices at the points \(z_1, z_2, \dots, z_n\). Determine the smallest value of \(n\) such that the area of \(P_n\) is at least 1000 times the area of \(P_1\).
What is the maximum integer value of $n$ for which $5 \cdot 4^{100} - 1$ is divisible by $3^n$?

Alice and Bob are playing a game with a sequence of positive integers \( a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{10} \). They take turns to choose an index \( i \) and change \( a_i \) to the sum of its two neighboring terms, i.e., \( a_i = a_{i-1} + a_{i+1} \) (except for the boundary terms \( a_1 \) and \( a_{10} \)). The game ends when the sum of all terms in the sequence becomes a perfect square. Determine the minimum possible value of \( a_1 + a_2 + \ldots + a_{10} \) such that the game is guaranteed to end.

In the coordinate plane, a regular hexagon \(ABCDEF\) is inscribed in a circle of radius \(2\). Let \(G\) be the midpoint of the line segment \(AB\), and let \(H\) be the midpoint of the line segment \(CD\). If the area of the hexagon can be expressed as \(k\sqrt{3}\), and the distance between \(G\) and \(H\) is \(\sqrt{l}\), where \(k\) and \(l\) are positive integers, find the value of \(k + l\).

Let \( n \) be the number of ways to color a 4 x 6 grid with four different colors such that no two adjacent squares (sharing a side) have the same color. Find the number of possible values for \( \lfloor \log_{8} n \rfloor \).

Let \( P(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( P(1) = 1 \) and \( P(2) = 2 \). Prove that for any prime number \( p \), the equation \( P(x) = p \) has at most two integer solutions.

Two convex polygons in the plane, \( A \) and \( B \), have a total of \( 2023 \) sides combined. \( A \) has more sides than \( B \), and neither polygon can be inscribed in a circle or circumscribed about a circle. Given that each pair of sides (one from \( A \) and one from \( B \)) forms a quadrilateral with exactly two distinct angles between them, determine the maximum number of sides polygon \( A \) can have.

A circle with radius 1 is drawn on a plane. A point P lies inside the circle such that the line segment from P to the center of the circle is a chord of length 2. What is the maximum possible area of a right triangle with one vertex at P and the other two vertices on the circumference of the circle?

In a plane, let \( S \) be a set of 100 points such that no three points are collinear and exactly one point is colored red. For each pair of points, draw the line segment connecting them. How many unique configurations of lines can be created such that every line segment passes through exactly one of these points or exactly one red point (excluding segments that contain the red point)?  Give your answer modulo 1,000,000,007.

We define a sequence of complex numbers $\{z_n\}$ as follows. For each positive integer $n$ , $\sum_{d\mid n} |z_d|=n$ and $|z_m|=m$ for all positive divisors $m$ of $n$ . Let $w$ be an arbitrary complex number, and define $z_n=w^{n+1}$. Determine all such $w$.

In the Cartesian plane, points \(A(0, 0)\) and \(B(10, 10)\) are given. Let \(C\) be a variable point on the circle centered at \(O(5, 0)\) with radius \(5\). Consider the locus of points \(D\) such that the area of triangle \(ACD\) is equal to the area of triangle \(BCD\). Find the minimum possible distance between point \(D\) and the origin \(O\).

In triangle \(ABC\), point \(P\) lies inside the triangle such that the cevians \(AP\), \(BP\), and \(CP\) intersect the opposite sides at points \(D\), \(E\), and \(F\) respectively. Suppose that \(PD = PE = PF\) and \(AD + BE + CF = DE + EF + FD\). Determine the ratio of the area of triangle \(ABC\) to the area of triangle \(DEF\).

Suppose there is a circular arrangement of n people, and each person is either a knight (always tells the truth) or a knave (always lies). If person i claims that person i + 1 is a knave, what is the probability that at least one person in the group is a knave, assuming an equal likelihood of each person being a knight or a knave?

A point moves inside a regular hexagon with side length 1, alternating between moving directly towards a randomly chosen vertex and moving directly towards the midpoint of a randomly chosen side. After 2023 such moves, what is the expected distance from the initial position to the final position?

Let \( a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{2023} \) be a sequence of positive integers such that for each \( k \geq 3 \), \( a_k \) is either the arithmetic mean, geometric mean, or harmonic mean of \( a_{k-1} \) and \( a_{k-2} \). Moreover, suppose \( a_{2023} = 2023 \). Find the number of possible values of \( a_1 + a_2 \).
What is the smallest positive integer that can be expressed as a difference of squares of two positive integers and is also a perfect cube?

Let \(ABC\) be a triangle with orthocenter \(H\), circumcenter \(O\), and incenter \(I\). Suppose that the circumradius is \(R\) and the inradius is \(r\). If \(AO = 3\) and \(r = 2\), determine the minimum possible integer value for \(AH\).

Consider a \( 100 \times 100 \) grid of unit squares. A **magic path** is a sequence of moves from one square to another, such that each move is either to the right, upwards, left, or downwards, and no square is visited more than once. If a magic path starts from the bottom-left corner square and ends at the top-right corner square, what is the maximum possible number of squares that can be visited by such a path?

Alice and Bob are playing a game with a fair six-sided die. Alice rolls the die and records the result as \( a \). Then, Bob rolls the die and records the result as \( b \). If the product \( a \times b \) is even, Alice wins. If \( a \times b \) is odd, Bob wins. They repeat this process \( n \) times, and the winner is the one with the most wins after these \( n \) rolls. If there is a tie, they roll once more to break it.

For what minimum number \( n \) of rolls is it possible that the probability of Alice winning is exactly \( \frac{2}{3} \)?

Consider a set \( S \) consisting of the integers from 1 to 20. Define a function \( f: S \times S \to \mathbb{Z} \) by \( f(a, b) = a^2 - b^2 \). Let \( T \) be the set of all possible outputs of \( f \) when \( a \) and \( b \) are chosen such that \( a > b \). Determine the number of distinct elements in \( T \).
Let $P(x) = x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d$ be a polynomial with real coefficients such that $P(1) = 17,$ $P(2) = 34,$ and $P(3) = 51.$ Compute $P(-1).$

Let \( n \) be a positive integer such that \( 1000 < \operatorname{rad}(n) < 2000 \), where \( \operatorname{rad}(n) \) is the largest prime factor of \( n \). Find the smallest possible value of \( \operatorname{rad}(n) \) and all such \( n \) that have at least \( 2 \) distinct positive divisors and do not contain squares other than \( 1 \) in their factorization.

A sequence \(\{a_n\}\) is defined as follows: \(a_1 = 1\) and for \(n \geq 1\), \(a_{n+1} = a_n^2 + a_n\). Define \(f(n)\) as the smallest positive integer \(m\) such that \(a_m\) is a multiple of \(2^n\). What is the value of \(f(20)\)?

Find all integers \( n \ge 2 \) such that there exists a polynomial \( P(x) = a_nx^n + \dots + a_1x + a_0 \) with integer coefficients such that:
- \( P(1) = 2018 \)
- For each positive integer \( k \ge 1 \), \(\sum_{d | k} P(d) = P(k) \)
answer: There are no integers \( n \ge 2 \) that satisfy the given conditions.

problem: In a regular octagon $ABCDEFGH$, let $P$ and $Q$ be points on sides $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{BC}$, respectively, such that $AP = BQ = CQ$. Find the measure of $\angle AQP$.

Alice writes all the positive integers from $1$ to $100$ on the blackboard. In one operation, she picks any two numbers, and replaces them with a new number. The new number is determined by the following rule: if the two numbers she picked are $x$ and $y$, then she writes down the number of positive divisors of $(x - y)^2$.

Alice performs operations until exactly one number is left on the board. What is the maximum possible value of the number that remains on the board after these operations?

There is a set of 2023 positive integers, none exceeding 2023, such that for any two numbers a and b (not necessarily distinct) from this set, the ratio a/b is also in the set.
Find the maximum number of elements of such a set.
What is the least value of the positive integer n such that in some subset of {n, n + 1, n + 2, ... , n + 799} with 1000 elements the sum of the members is divisible by 2000?

In a particular game, three players, Alpha, Beta, and Gamma, start with 3, 4, and 5 points, respectively. The game has a unique rule: at each turn, the player with the most points can transfer 1 point to the player with the least points. The game ends when all players have the same number of points. What is the minimum number of turns required to achieve this condition, and who will be the first player to transfer the points?

Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be real numbers such that $a + b + c = 0$. Define the polynomial $P(x) = (x^2 + ax + b)(x^2 + bx + c)(x^2 + cx + a)$. Find all possible values of $a^2 + b^2 + c^2$ if it is known that $P(x)$ has exactly two distinct real roots.

Alice and Bob play a game on a grid of size 5x5. Alice starts by placing a token on any cell of the grid. On each turn, a player can move the token to an adjacent cell (up, down, left, or right, but not diagonally) and then paint that cell black. Alice wins if she can create a path of black cells from the top row to the bottom row without ever leaving the grid. Bob wins if he can prevent Alice from creating such a path after 15 moves. Who has a winning strategy?

Let \( f(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients. Suppose \( f(x) \) has exactly two distinct integer roots and no other integer roots. If \( f(0) = 17 \), find the smallest possible positive value of \( f(1) \).

Suppose \( f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} \) is a function such that for any real numbers \( x > y \), the following holds:
\[ \frac{f(x) + f(y)}{f(x - y)} = 2023. \]
Determine the value of \( f(2024) \).

On a circular track of length 1000 meters, 100 athletes start at the same point. Each athlete runs at a constant speed, but their speeds are all distinct and are integers in meters per second. After some time \( t \), every athlete has passed every other athlete exactly once. Determine the maximum possible value of \( t \).

The chocolate frosting problem states the following:
Alice & Bob playing a two person game. Each turn Alice starts by choosing a nonnegative integer k and Bob ends by choosing a nonnegative integer l.
Alice's move: Choose a nonnegative integer k from any previously chosen integers, meaning l if l is the last number chosen.
Bob's move: Choose a nonnegative integer l from any previously chosen integers, meaning k if k is the last number chosen.
The game stops if a player chooses a number l such that for all integers a,b,c,d such that a + b = 3k and c + d = 3l, then a + c = b + d. They were trying to figure out the maximum amount of numbers that could be played.
How many integers can the game last?
The game ends when one person chooses a number such that no integer satisfies k(a,b,c,d).

For a positive integer $n$, let $f(n)$ denote the sum of its positive divisors, including 1 and $n$ itself. We call $n$ "friendly" if $f(n) + f(f(n)) = n + f(n)$ is divisible by both $n$ and $f(n)$. How many friendly integers less than 1000 are there?

Let \( P(x) = x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d \) be a polynomial with real coefficients. Suppose that for all real numbers \( x \), \( P(x) \) and its derivative \( P'(x) \) have the same sign (either both positive or both negative). Determine the maximum number of distinct real roots that \( P(x) \) can have.

There are five noncollinear points in a plane. How many ways can you draw two circles, each passing through four of the points but excluding all other points, such that the second circle excludes at least one point of the first?

Let $f(x)$ be a function defined on $\mathbb{R}$ such that for all real numbers $x$, the following conditions hold:
\[f(1 + x) = 1 + f(x) \quad \text{and} \quad f\left( \frac{1}{x} \right) = \frac{f(x)}{x^2},\]
where $x \neq 0$. If $f(1) = 1$, find the value of $f(i)$, where $i$ is the imaginary unit.

Let \( P(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( P(0) = 1 \) and \( P(1) = 2023 \). Suppose that there exists an integer \( k \) such that \( P(k) \) is divisible by 2023. If \( n \) is the smallest positive integer for which \( P(n) \) is divisible by 2023, determine the largest possible value of \( n \).

Alice and Bob are playing a game with a pile of stones. The game starts with 100 stones. On each turn, a player must remove at least one stone, and they cannot remove a number of stones that is a multiple of 5. The player who removes the last stone wins. If Alice goes first, what is the smallest number of stones she must remove to ensure she wins the game?

Consider a \(2023 \times 2023\) grid. An integer from \(1\) to \(2023\) is assigned to each cell such that each integer is used exactly \(2023\) times. For each row, choose the number that appears most frequently in that row. Let \(X\) be the sum of these \(2023\) numbers. Similarly, for each column, choose the number that appears most frequently in that column. Let \(Y\) be the sum of these \(2023\) numbers. Compute the maximum possible value of \(X + Y\).

Alice writes 2011 distinct positive integers on a board. She calculates the greatest common divisor (GCD) of each pair of adjacent numbers, obtaining 2010 different GCDs. What is the minimum number of these 2010 GCDs that must be even?
What is the remainder when $11^{2023} + 13^{2023}$ is divided by $100$?

There are 1000 doors marked 1 through 1000. One hundred people are each assigned to a number from 1 to 100. Person 1 starts at door 1 and goes to every multiple of 1, person 2 starts at door 2 and goes to every multiple of 2, and so on. Person i goes to the door(s) numbered as the multiples of their assigned number. If a person finds the door open, they close it. If it is closed, they open it. After all 100 people have followed this process, which doors are left open? Prove that your answer is correct.

Among the permutations \(\{1, 2, \dots, 99\} \to \{1, 2, \dots, 99\}\), how many can be divided into \(33\) disjoint cycles whose lengths add to \(99\), in such a way that the sum of the lengths of cycles with odd sums of elements is \(51\) and the sum of the lengths of cycles with even sums of elements is \(48\)?
What is the smallest possible value of \[x^2 + 8x + \frac{64}{x^3}\]for positive real numbers $x$?

Consider the sequence of positive integers where each term is defined as the sum of the squares of the digits of the previous term. For instance, starting with 12, the next term is \(1^2 + 2^2 = 5\), followed by \(5^2 = 25\), and then \(2^2 + 5^2 = 29\). Determine the smallest starting integer \(n\) for which this sequence eventually reaches the number 1 and does not exceed 100 before doing so.

Let \( P(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( P(0) = 1 \) and \( P(1) = 2 \). Suppose that for some integer \( k \), the polynomial \( P(x) - k \) has at least three distinct integer roots. Determine the maximum possible value of \( k \).

Consider a sequence of integers \(a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_{100}\) where each \(a_n\) is defined as the sum of the first \(n\) positive integers squared, i.e., \(a_n = \sum_{k=1}^n k^2\). Let \(S\) be the sum of all the distinct prime factors of \(a_{100}\). What is the value of \(S\)?
What is the smallest positive integer \( k \) such that \( 1000k \) is a factor of \( 2003! \)?

In the complex plane, the circles \\(|z| = 2\\) and \\(|z - 3| = 1\\) intersect at points \\(A\\) and \\(B\\). Let \\(C\\) be the complex number \\(1 + 3i\\). Find the magnitude of the complex number \\(z\\) such that \\(z = \\overline{C} + AC \cdot AB\\).

A regular octagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 10. Points \(A\) and \(B\) are chosen on two non-adjacent sides of the octagon such that the lines \(OA\) and \(OB\) intersect the circle at points \(A'\) and \(B'\) respectively, where \(O\) is the center of the circle. If the line segment \(AB\) is parallel to the line segment \(A'B'\), what is the length of the segment \(AB\)?

There are 4 players (A, B, C, and D) playing a game. In each round, two players are randomly chosen to play against each other. The chosen players play until one of them wins. The winner continues to play in the next round against a player who has not yet been matched with them in any previous rounds. If all players have been matched with each other, the player with the least number of matches played so far is chosen to play in the next round. After 6 rounds, what is the probability that player A has won exactly 2 rounds? Express your answer as a common fraction.

You are given a deck of 52 playing cards, of which exactly one card is red, and the rest are blue. The cards are shuffled so that the probability of drawing any given card is 1/52. You draw two cards at random, one at a time without replacement. If the second card is red, what is the probability that the first card was also red?

Consider a polynomial \(P(x) = x^n + a_1x^{n-1} + a_2x^{n-2} + \dots + a_n\) with integer coefficients and \(n \geq 3\), where \(a_n \neq 0\). Define a sequence \(\{b_k\}\) such that \(b_0 = 0\) and for all \(k \geq 1\),
\[b_k = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} P(b_i).\]
Prove that there exists a positive integer \(N\) such that for all \(n \geq N\), if \(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n\) are distinct, then there exists a positive integer \(k < 2024\) for which \(b_k\) is divisible by \(2023\).

A flea starts at the origin of the Cartesian plane. Every minute, it can perform the following sequence of operations in any order: move 1 unit to the right or to the left, or double its own coordinates. What is the smallest number of minutes after which the flea can reach the point (2023, 2024)?

Consider a sequence of positive integers \( a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n \) such that \( a_{i+1} \) is the smallest positive integer greater than \( a_i \) that is relatively prime to \( a_i \) and has not appeared in the sequence before. If \( a_1 = 2 \), what is the maximum number of distinct integers in the sequence up to the 100th term?

Let \( S \) be the set of all positive integers \( n \) for which \( \frac{1}{n} \) has the repeating decimal representation
\[
\frac{1}{n} = 0.\overline{a_1a_2a_3\ldots a_{12}}
\]
where \( a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_{12} \) are not necessarily distinct digits and \( n \) is the smallest integer for which \( \frac{1}{n} \) has a repeating period of exactly 12 digits. Determine \( n \).

A number  𝑛  
n  is called *ambiguous* if, when expressed in base 10, the product of its digits is exactly twice its sum. How many ambiguous numbers exist below 1000?

Alice and Bob are playing a game on a tree consisting of n vertices (vertices are numbered from 1 to n ). The edges of the tree are undirected.

Initially, all vertices contain 0, except for the root vertex which contains the integer a1 .

On each step, Alice selects a vertex v with the maximum number (could be equal to several vertices, in which case she can choose any of them). Then she selects an edge e from the vertex v (vertex v must not be a leaf). Then the following sequence of events happen:

let c be the number of vertices connected to vertex v by edge e in the original tree;
the number c is subtracted from all selected vertices v;
the number 0 is added to all other vertices.
Alice's friend Bob is trying to distract her by asking her q questions, each in the form l r . For each question, Alice should print the vertex number with the largest value on the interval [l,r] .

Help Alice cheat Bob. Her advantage is that she can query Alice herself during the game, and she can recall the answer to a question any time before she answers Bob's question. Alice's disadvantage is that Bob gives her queries one by one, and when he gives a query, she has to answer it immediately, and otherwise Bob can cheat her.

Bob wants to minimize the number of queries that Alice needs to do. Alice wants to minimize the number of queries she needs to do while managing to answer Bob's questions. What's the minimum number of queries Alice has to do given that both of them try to reach their goals?

Input
The first line contains two integers n , q (1≤n≤200000, 1≤q≤105) — the number of vertices and the number of questions, respectively.

The second line contains n integers a1 , a2 ,... an (1≤ai≤107) — the initial numbers of the vertices in the tree.

The next n−1 lines contain descriptions of the edges of the tree, one edge per line. The i-th line contains two integers vi , ui (1≤vi,ui≤n, vi≠ui) — the numbers of vertices connected by the i-th edge.

The next line contains q integers b1 , b2 ,... bq (1≤bj≤n) — the integers Bob gives to Alice as the questions.

It is guaranteed that the given graph is a tree.

Output
Print one integer t (0≤t≤105) — the minimum number of queries Alice has to do to answer all questions from Bob.

Example
Input
4 3
1 10 100 1000
1 2
2 3
2 4
1 3 4
Output
3
Note
One of the possible solutions: 

Alice queries [2,2], then queries [2,4], and then queries [1,4].

Then Alice manages to answer all Bob's questions. Indeed: after the first query, vertex 1 contains the number 1000, vertex 2 contains the number 1000, vertex 3 contains the number 800, and vertex 4 contains the number 800. So in the first question, Bob asks about a vertex with the maximum value, and it's vertex 1.

After the second query, vertex 1 contains the number 1000, vertex 2 contains the number 600, vertex 3 contains the number 600, and vertex 4 contains the number 400. So in the second question, Bob asks about the vertex with the maximum value, and it is vertex 1 again. Alice answers it without another query, because the value of vertex 1 is obviously greater than the value of vertex 3.

After the third query, vertex 1 contains the number 1000, vertex 2 contains the number 300, vertex 3 contains the number 300, and vertex 4 contains the number 100. So in the second question, Bob asks about the vertex with the maximum value, and it is vertex 1 again. Alice answers it without another query, because the value of vertex 1 is obviously greater than the value of vertex 4.

Thus, Alice had to do 3 queries to give all Bob's answers.
What is the remainder when (3^100 + 4^(100) + 2^(100)) ^ 3 is divided by 7?

An integer partition of a number $n$ is a sequence of integers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_m$, with $a_1 \ge a_2 \ge \dots \ge a_m$ and $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_m = n$. A partition is *primitive* if it contains no repeating integers. We define $r(n)$ as the number of primitive partitions of $n$ that do not contain the integer $2$. For example, $r(9) = 4$, as the four primitive partitions are $\{9\}, \{3, 6\}, \{5, 4\}, \{7, 2\}$. Let $R(N)$ be the sum of $r(n)$ for $n$ from $2$ to $N$. Find the last 18 digits of $R(10^{15})$.

A rectangular floor is covered in square tiles. The tiles are of two colors: red and blue. There are 18 red tiles, and the number of blue tiles is 4 times the number of red tiles. The length of the floor is 32 tiles and the width is 24 tiles. What is the probability of choosing a blue tile at random from all the tiles on the floor?

Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients. It is known that there exist distinct integers $a, b, c$ such that $P(a) = b$, $P(b) = c$, and $P(c) = a$. Find all possible values of the integer $d$ such that $P(d) = d$.
What is the minimum length of the chord on the unit circle that can be cut by a line that intersects both the unit circle and the ellipse $x^2/4 + y^2/9 = 1$?
In a regular heptagon (7-sided polygon), how many diagonals can be drawn such that no three diagonals are concurrent at a single point inside the heptagon? Provide your answer modulo 1000.

Alice and Bob take turns writing integers from 1 to 100 on a chalkboard. Each integer written by Alice must be a perfect square, while Bob's integers must be prime numbers. They start with Alice, and whoever writes the number that causes the sum of all numbers on the board to exceed 5000 loses. If both Alice and Bob play optimally, who has a winning strategy?

Five students, Alice, Bob, Carol, Dave, and Eve, participate in a math contest where they earn points for each correct answer. Before the contest starts, they make the following statements:
- Alice: "I know I will score more points than Dave."
- Bob: "Eve will score fewer points than I will."
- Carol: "I scored less than Dave."
- Dave: "Carol scored less than I did, and I expect my score will exceed Eve's."
- Eve: "I don't know my score, but I did not score the most points."

If all students are lying, and each student has a distinct integer score from 1 to 5 points (with no fractional points), what is the sum of the scores of Dave and Eve?

For positive integers \(m\) and \(n\), define the operation \(m \ast n\) such that \(m \ast n = \frac{mn - m - n}{5}\). How many ordered triples \((a, b, c)\) of positive integers satisfy both \(a \ast b = c\) and \(b \ast c = a\)?

In the plane, let \\( P_0 \\) be the line \\( x - y = 0 \\). For every integer \\( n \ge 1 \\), \\( P_n \\) is a line with x-intercept \\( a_n \\) and y-intercept \\( b_n \\) such that \\( a_n + b_n = -4 \\). It is also true that \\( P_0 \bot P_1 \bot \ldots \bot P_n \bot \ldots \\). Let \\( (x_n, y_n) \\) be the infinite sequence of points where line \\( P_n \\) intersects line \\( P_{n+1} \\) for \\( n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots \\). Find \\( x_n + y_n \\) in terms of \\( n \\).

There are 100 people in a classroom. Some number of them always tell the truth, and the rest always lie. Among these people, there is exactly one person who is always a liar and always tells the truth. If any person is asked to say what the total number of people in the room is, he or she will answer a number between 50 and 200 inclusive. What is the minimum number of people in the room who must always lie?

(A) 33

(B) 34

(C) 35

(D) 36

(E) 37

A sequence of positive integers \((a_n)_{n\geq1}\) is defined by the recurrence relation \(a_{n+2} = 2a_{n+1} + a_n\) for all \(n \geq 1\), with initial conditions \(a_1 = 1\) and \(a_2 = 3\). Let \(S_k = a_1 + a_2 + \ldots + a_k\). Determine the smallest positive integer \(k\) such that \(S_k\) is a perfect square.

In an isosceles triangle \( ABC \) with \( AB = AC \), points \( D \) and \( E \) are on \( AB \) and \( AC \), respectively, such that \( AD = AE \). Suppose \( \angle BAC = 36^\circ \). If \( AB = 1 \), calculate the length \( DE \) in the form \( \frac{1 - \sqrt{x}}{y} \). Find the product \( x \cdot y \).

Alice and Bob are playing a game on an infinite grid. They start at the origin (0, 0). Each turn, Alice moves to a point that is exactly 1 unit away from her current position in any direction (up, down, left, right, or diagonally), and then Bob moves to a point that is exactly 2 units away from Alice's current position in any direction. If Bob can reach Alice's original starting position (0, 0) at any point during the game, he wins. Otherwise, Alice wins. After Alice's first move, she can prevent Bob from winning. What is the minimum number of moves Alice must make to ensure she wins the game?

A convex polygon has its vertices colored using three colors: red, blue, and green. It's known that no two adjacent vertices have the same color, and there exists at least one vertex for each color. Let \( n_r \) denote the number of vertices colored red. If the polygon has a total of \( n \) vertices, determine the maximum possible value for the expression
\[ S = n_r + \left( \frac{n}{2} - n_r \right) \left( \frac{1}{2} - \frac{n_r}{n} \right) \]
as a function of \( n \). Prove that your expression gives the maximum value.

Find all positive integers \( n \) such that the equation
\[ n x^{2} - (n+1) x + n + 3 = 0 \]
has roots that are integers.

Let \( P(x) \) be a polynomial with real coefficients such that \( P(x) = P(-x) \) for all \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). If \( P(1) = 2023 \) and \( P(x) \) has exactly four distinct real roots, determine the maximum number of integer values that can be roots of \( P(x) \).

There are  $n$  cards, each has a number on one side and the reverse side of the card is white. Some cards have a positive number and some of them have a negative number on it and the rest have  $0$  on it. In addition, we have a magic device that does the following:

$\bullet$  If two distinct cards with non-zero numbers are selected, it swaps the numbers of the cards, if the numbers have different signs.

$\bullet$  If two distinct cards with non-zero numbers are selected and the numbers have the same signs, it determines with  $100 \%$  accuracy, whether there is a positive number on both cards and if so, it changes the color of the reverse side of both cards to red. The magic device never changes the color of the reverse side of the cards.

Let  $k \leq n$ . Suppose that you can see the numbers on the reverse side of  $k$  cards. Determine the maximum value of  $k$  such that the following holds: There exists a strategy that after it is carried out, for any initial configuration, you can determine the numbers on all cards, or you can achieve a configuration in which at least one of the red cards has a positive number on it.

Also, describe a strategy with that value of  $k$  that works.
The base of a triangle is 10 cm, and the altitude to this base is 6 cm. Calculate the area of the triangle.

Let \( f(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( f(0) = 1 \) and \( f(1) = 2 \). Suppose \( f(x) \) has a root \( r \) that is an algebraic integer. If \( r \) is a root of the polynomial \( g(x) = x^3 - 3x + 1 \), find the minimum possible degree of \( f(x) \).

Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ with real coefficients. Suppose that for all real numbers $x,$ the polynomial $Q(x) = P(x) + 3x^3 + 4x$ satisfies the condition that $|Q(x)| \leq 1$ for $-1 \leq x \leq 1.$ Determine the maximum possible value of $n.$
What is the smallest positive integer $n$ such that $n^2+400$ is a perfect square, $n$ is even, and $n$ is not divisible by 3?

What is the minimum number of colors required to color all the squares on an 8 by 8 chessboard, given that each pair of squares that share a common edge must be of different colors, and no two squares that are diagonally adjacent can be of the same color?

Points \( A_0 \), \( B_0 \), and \( C_0 \) are on sides \( BC \), \( CA \), and \( AB \) of a triangle \( ABC \), respectively, so that \( BC_0 : C_0A = CA_0 : A_0B = AB_0 : B_0C = 1 : 3 \). Determine the ratio of the area of triangle \( A_0B_0C_0 \) to the area of triangle \( ABC \). Express your answer as a common fraction.

Let \( n \) be a positive integer. A set \( S \) of positive integers is called *hyper-sum-free* if there do not exist \( a, b, c \in S \) (not necessarily distinct) such that \( a + b = c \) and \( a \leq b \leq c \). Determine the smallest possible size of a hyper-sum-free set that contains all positive integers from 1 to \( n \).

In a geometric configuration, consider a circle with radius 10 units. A point P is chosen inside the circle such that the sum of the distances from P to the circle's circumference is minimized. What is the shortest possible sum of these distances? Express your answer in simplest radical form.

Let \( P(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( P(0) = 1 \) and \( P(1) = 2 \). Suppose that \( P(x) \) has the property that for every integer \( k \), \( P(k) \) is a multiple of \( k^2 + k + 1 \). Determine the maximum possible degree of \( P(x) \).

Let \( f(x) \) be a polynomial of degree \( n \) with integer coefficients such that \( f(0) = 1 \) and \( f(k) \equiv 0 \pmod{p} \) for all prime numbers \( p \) less than or equal to \( k \). Determine the maximum possible value of \( n \).
Among all the rectangles with vertices on the edge of an ellipse, what is the minimal number of lattice points with integer coordinates their vertices can form in the coordinate plane?

You are given a regular tetrahedron with vertices labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4. Each face of the tetrahedron is to be painted a different color: red, blue, green, or yellow. How many distinct colorings are possible, where colorings that can be rotated to match each other are considered the same?

In a circle with radius \( r \), consider a chord of length \( 2r \) which subtends an angle of \( 120^\circ \) at the center. Points \( A \) and \( B \) are chosen on this chord such that \( AB \) is also a diameter of the circle. Determine the area of the quadrilateral formed by the points where the perpendicular bisectors of \( AB \) and the chord intersect the circumference of the circle.
What is the maximum number of rational distances that can exist between any ten points in the plane?

Consider a polynomial $P(x)$ of degree 2023 with integer coefficients such that $P(0) = 2023$. Let $Q(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients satisfying $Q(x)^2 + Q(x) = P(x)^2 + P(x)$. Determine the maximum possible number of integer roots of $Q(x)$.

Let \( S \) be the set of all positive integers that have an even number of digits and can be split into two parts \( A \) and \( B \) such that \( A + B \) is a perfect square and \( B \) is a prime number. For example, 1372 is in \( S \) because \( 13 + 72 = 85 \) is not a perfect square, but \( 137 + 2 = 139 \) is a perfect square and 2 is a prime number. What is the smallest number in \( S \)?

You have a sequence of positive integers \(a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n\) such that the product of any two consecutive terms is divisible by the sum of these two terms. If \(a_1 = 1\) and \(a_{10} = 2023\), find the smallest possible value of \(n\).
There are 2015 marbles in a bag. 132 marbles are white, 668 are green and the rest are red. If you take a marble from the bag at random what are the chances the marble is red? A

Alice is playing a game on an infinite 2D grid. Initially, she is at the origin \((0,0)\). Each turn, she can move to any adjacent lattice point (up, down, left, or right). After each move, the value of her current position \((x,y)\) is updated to \(x^2 + y^2\). Alice wins if she reaches a position whose value is a perfect square greater than or equal to 100. Determine if there exists a strategy for Alice to win, and if so, provide the minimum number of moves required to achieve this.
What is the remainder when \(\sum_{n=1}^{20} n^n\) is divided by 5?

Let \( P(x) \) be a monic polynomial with integer coefficients of degree 4 such that \( P(0) = 1 \) and \( P(x) \) has four distinct integer roots. Define the sequence \( \{a_n\} \) by \( a_0 = 0 \), \( a_1 = 1 \), and \( a_{n+2} = a_{n+1} + a_n + a_{n-1} \) for \( n \geq 0 \). Find the smallest positive integer \( n \) such that \( a_n \) divides \( P(2023) \).

On a circular track divided into 120 equal segments numbered from 1 to 120 clockwise, two runners start at segment 1. Runner A runs clockwise at 5 segments per second, while Runner B runs counter-clockwise at 9 segments per second. They begin running simultaneously. Determine the number of segments from segment 1 when they first meet after their initial start.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $E$ be a point on $AC$ such that $DE \parallel AB$. Let $F$ be a point on $AB$ such that $EF \parallel BC$. Let $G$ be the intersection of $DE$ and $BC$. Let $H$ be the intersection of $EF$ and $AC$. If $DG = 1$, $DH = 2$, and $EF = 3$, find the length of $GH$.

In a certain two-dimensional lattice, each point \((x, y)\) is connected to its four neighbors by unit-length lines. Consider a path from \((0, 0)\) to \((n, n)\) that consists of \(2n\) steps, each moving one unit either right or up. A path is considered *valid* if it does not pass through any point \((a, a)\) for \(0 < a < n\).

Let \(P(n)\) denote the number of valid paths from \((0, 0)\ to \((n, n)\). Determine the value of \(P(2023)\).

Let \(P(x)\) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \(P(1) = 2\) and \(P(2) = 3\). Suppose there exists a positive integer \(n\) such that \(P(n) = n!\) (where \(n!\) denotes the factorial of \(n\)). Determine the minimum possible value of \(n\).

Let's consider an eight-digit natural number where the first and last digits are 5, and the digit in the fifth place is 3. If this number is a prime number, how many different values can the seventh digit take?

Let \( f(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( f(21) = 17, \) \( f(32) = -247, \) and \( f(37) = 33. \) Let \( r(x) \) be the polynomial remainder when \( f(x) \) is divided by \( x^3 - x^2 - 6x + 8. \) Find \( r(5). \)

Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial with real coefficients and degree $n$. If the sum of the $n$th powers of the roots of $f(x)$ is equal to the product of the $n$th powers of the roots of $f(x)$, then find all possible values of $n$.

In a mathematical game, Alice and Bob take turns choosing a positive integer, starting with Alice. The rules are as follows:
1. The first player to choose a number must pick a number greater than 1 that is a multiple of 3.
2. Each subsequent player must choose a number that is a multiple of the previous number and also a multiple of 3.
3. The game continues until a player is unable to choose a valid number that satisfies the rules.

If Alice starts by choosing 3 and both players play optimally, what is the smallest number that Bob can choose on his first turn?

In the complex plane, the polynomial \( P(z) = z^4 + az^3 + bz^2 + cz + d \) has roots \( r_1, r_2, r_3, r_4 \) such that \( r_1 + r_2 = 2 \) and \( r_3 + r_4 = 4 \). If \( r_1r_2 + r_3r_4 = 3 \), find the value of \( a + b + c + d \).
In a convex hexagon $ABCDEF$, $AB$ is parallel to $DE$ and $BC$ is parallel to $EF$. If $\angle B = 125^\circ$ and $\angle F = 80^\circ$, find $\angle D$.

Suppose that \( f \) is a function defined on the set of integers, such that \( f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y) + f(xy) \) for all integers \( x \) and \( y \). Given that \( f(1) = 3 \), find the value of \( f(7) \).

What is the minimum number of pegs you have to leave in the board such that no matter how two other players move their pegs, you can always move your own peg, so that no one has a win, assuming the following configuration, with your peg labeled as Y, and the other two players’ pegs labeled as R and B respectively:

X X X
X Y X
X X X

There are six people sitting in a circle, each with a unique number from 1 to 6. They decide to play a game where each person can only see the numbers of their immediate neighbors. They are told that the sum of all six numbers is 21. In one round, each person can make one statement based only on the information they can see. However, no one can see their own number. After three rounds, what is the smallest possible number that could be on the person who sits directly between the people numbered 3 and 5?

For positive integers \( n \), let \( P_n = \frac{n(n+1)}{2} \) represent the \( n \)-th triangular number, and let \( S_n = P_n^2 - n \). How many positive integers \( n \leq 2023 \) are there for which \( S_n \) is a perfect square?

Alice, Bob, and Carol decide to play a game with an unbiased coin. They agree to flip the coin multiple times, but instead of using a pre-determined rule for each player, they will follow the following scheme:

1. The first two consecutive heads (HH) will be owned by Alice.
2. If heads (H) follow by tails (T) after two consecutive heads (HTH), Bob will own them.
3. If the next two flips are tails (TH), it will continue from the next flip.
4. The cycle repeats.

They stop the game when all three players have owned exactly 4 instances of each combination. How many total coin flips are expected when the game stops?

Let \( P(x) \) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \( P(0) = 1 \) and \( P(1) = 2023 \). Suppose further that for every prime number \( p \), \( P(p) \) is also a prime number. Prove that there exists a positive integer \( n \) such that for all prime numbers \( q \geq n \), \( P(q) \equiv 1 \pmod{q} \).

Masha and Slava are taking turns selecting integers in ascending order from 1 to 50,000 inclusive (starting with Masha). Each number is picked exactly once. The loser is the one who gets stuck at the number 1. Let’s introduce a strict turn penalty: if player X has the last move, they lose 1 point; if the last move is made by player Y, they lose 2 points. They each start with an initial score of 0 points. What is the highest possible score difference they can end with?
What is the probability that a randomly selected positive integer less than 1,000,000, when its digits are rearranged, is still a positive integer less than 1,000,000?

Find the greatest integer \( n \) for which there exist positive integers \( a \), \( b \), \( c \), and \( d \) such that 
\[
n = \frac{a^3 + b^3 + c^3 + d^3}{1 + abcd}
\]
and the polynomial \( x^4 - nx^3 + n \) has a rational root.
The sequence \((a_n)\) is defined by \(a_1 = 1\) and for \(n \ge 1\), \(a_{n+1} = \frac{a_n + 2023}{1 + a_n}\). Determine the smallest integer \(N\) such that \(a_N > 2023\).

Let $P(x) = x^{2023} + a_{2022}x^{2022} + \dots + a_1x + a_0$ be a polynomial with real coefficients. Suppose that for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the value of $P(x)$ is strictly between $-2023$ and $2023$ inclusive. Determine the maximum possible value of $|a_0| + |a_1| + \dots + |a_{2022}|$.

Let a_1, a_2, ..., a_{2023} be real numbers such that |a_i| < 1 for all i. Prove that there exists a subset of these numbers with at least 1012 elements such that the absolute value of their sum is less than or equal to 1.\
**What is the lowest possible value of \(|z|\) if \(z\) is a root of the equation \(z^8 + z^4 - z^2 + 1 = 0\)?

Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, and $e$ be distinct, non-zero real numbers such that
\[a + \frac{1}{b} = b + \frac{1}{c} = c + \frac{1}{d} = d + \frac{1}{e} = e + \frac{1}{a}.\]Find the absolute value of $abcde$.

In the Cartesian plane, the curve \(y = x^4 - 4x^2 + 4\) intersects the x-axis at three distinct points, which are the vertices of a triangle. Let \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) be these points with \(A\) having the smallest x-coordinate. Compute the area of the triangle \(ABC\).

Let $P(x)$ be a monic polynomial with integer coefficients such that $P(0)=1$. Suppose that for every positive integer $n$, the values $P(1), P(2), \ldots, P(n)$ are all divisible by a prime number $q_n$ that is not equal to $q_m$ for any $m < n$. Determine the smallest possible degree of $P(x)$.

Alice has written an integer in each square of an  $8 \times 8$  grid. The integer written in the rightmost square of the bottom row is  $0$ , and the other integers are nonzero. In each step, Alice chooses two adjacent squares sharing a common side and replaces the integers  $a, b$  in these squares by  $a^2 - ab + b^2$ . She repeats this process until every square contains the integer  $x$ . What are the possible values of  $x$ ?

Alice and Bob play a game with a polynomial P(x) = ax^4 + bx^3 + cx^2 + dx + e, where all coefficients a, b, c, d, and e are non-negative integers less than 10. They take turns picking a natural number n, and Alice wins if P(n) is divisible by 10. Assuming optimal play, what is the largest possible value of e that guarantees Alice a win?
James and Mary agree to play a game where they will flip a fair coin repeatedly, with James going first, and the first to flip a head wins. Find the probability that Mary wins.

Alice and Bob are playing a game with a deck of cards numbered from 1 to 100. They take turns drawing cards without replacement. The game ends when one player draws a card that is the sum of any two previously drawn cards. The player who draws this card loses. If Alice draws first, what is the highest card number that guarantees she will not lose the game on her turn?

Let $P(x)$ be a monic polynomial with integer coefficients such that $P(0) = 1$ and $P(1) = 3$. If $P(x)$ has at least one integer root, find the smallest possible value of $n$ for which $P(x)$ can be expressed as a product of at least $n$ non-constant polynomials with integer coefficients.

An 8 by 8 grid of squares is filled in with the digits 1 through 8 such that every row, column, and 2 by 2 sub-grid (there are 18 of them) contains each digit exactly once. If the sum of all digits in the grid is 290, what is the digit in the center square?

(A) 4
(B) 5
(C) 6
(D) 7
(E) 8

On the 13-circle plane where each circle is tangent to its neighbors, a game of dominoes is being played. Each player has an equal number of tiles, and each tile represents a domino piece that spans two adjacent circles. A move is defined as placing a tile that does not overlap any other tile and is tangent to its neighboring circles. Assuming the initial domino piece is already placed, what is the maximum number of consecutive moves a player can make without repeating any tiles or leaving any adjacent circles unoccupied?

Imagine a 2024-gon with 2024 sides where each interior angle is 179 degrees. If we pick any two adjacent sides, cut out the rectangle that forms with the two sides and the edges opposite to them on the polygon, and put this new smaller rectangle into another plane without rotating, how many such small rectangles can fit into a square of side length 2024?

Let \( ABC \) be an acute-angled triangle with circumcenter \( O \). The circle through \( B \) and \( C \) with center \( O \) intersects \( AB \) and \( AC \) again at points \( D \) and \( E \) respectively. Suppose that \( BD = CE \). Let \( M \) be the midpoint of \( BC \), and let \( N \) be the intersection of \( AM \) and \( DE \). If \( AN \cdot AM = 144 \), compute the area of \( \triangle BOC \).

Let \( P(x) \) be a monic polynomial of degree 2023 with real coefficients such that all its roots are non-zero and non-integer. Moreover, for each integer \( k \) with \( 1 \leq k \leq 2023 \), \( P(k) \) is an integer. Determine the maximum number of distinct integer roots that \( P(x) \) can have.

Let $S$ be a set of 1000 distinct positive integers. For each non-empty subset $T$ of $S$, let $M(T)$ denote the maximum of the elements in $T$. Let $N$ be the average value of $M(T)$ over all non-empty subsets $T$ of $S$. If the sum of the elements of $S$ is 1001000, find the smallest possible value of $N$.

Let \(ABC\) be a scalene triangle with circumcenter \(O\) and centroid \(G\). Let \(P\) be a point inside \(ABC\) such that \(AGOP\) is a parallelogram. A line through \(P\) parallel to \(BC\) intersects \(AB\) at \(X\) and \(AC\) at \(Y\). Given that \(XY = 20\) and \(BC = 30\), find \(\lfloor 1000 \cdot (XY + BC) \cdot \cos\angle XPG \rfloor\).

Consider a sequence of \( n \) non-negative integers \( a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n \) such that their sum is \( n \). A subsequence of these integers is considered "maximally non-decreasing" if it is either the empty sequence or the sum of its elements is strictly increasing. Given a function \( f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \) defined by \( f(k) = \max(1, k - 1) \), find the smallest \( n \) such that for any such sequence, there exists a maximally non-decreasing subsequence of length at least \( f(n) \).

Hint: Consider the Erdős-Szekeres theorem, and think about how you can apply it to this problem.

Alice and Bob play a game with an n x n grid of cells, where n is a positive integer. Initially, all cells are empty. On each turn, Alice places a "red" domino (2 adjacent cells) on an empty cell, and then Bob places a "blue" domino (2 adjacent cells) on an empty cell. Alice goes first. The game ends when no more dominoes can be placed. A "domino train" is a sequence of dominoes such that each domino shares at least one cell with the next domino in the sequence. Alice wins if, at the end of the game, the maximum length of a domino train she has formed is at least 3 times the maximum length of a domino train Bob has formed. For which values of n does Alice have a winning strategy?

What is the maximum number of non-overlapping equilateral triangles that can be inscribed in a regular octagon? Note that two triangles are considered non-overlapping if they do not share any interior points.

There are  $n$  students participating in a test. Each question of the test can be solved by at most  $5$  students. For each pair of students, there exists a question that are both of them unable to solve. Find the maximum value of  $n$ .

A sequence of numbers is defined by the following rules: 
1. \( a_1 = 2 \), 
2. For \( n \geq 2 \), \( a_n \) is the smallest positive integer not in the set \(\{a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{n-1}\}\) that is coprime with \( a_{n-1} \). 
Determine the 10th term of this sequence, \( a_{10} \).

Ivan is a farmer in the drylands of Africa, where he plants 100 seeds at the beginning of a new year. Unfortunately, each year, exactly one-third of all the remaining seeds will not grow due to weather conditions. At the start of the second year, Ivan plants 20 more seeds. This 20 seed improvement allows him to make up for the missing grains from the first year. At the start of the third year, Ivan plants 30 seeds. This third batch of seeds makes Ivan so successful that the crops grow significantly in the third year. How many crops did Ivan have at the start of the third year after planting these additional 30 seeds? Express your answer as a common fraction.

Alice and Bob play a game with a sequence of integers. Alice starts by writing a sequence \( a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n \) on a blackboard. On each turn, a player may choose any \( a_i \) such that \( a_i > a_{i+1} \) and replace \( a_i \) with \( a_i - a_{i+1} \). The game ends when no more moves can be made. Alice wins if the final sequence has at least one zero; otherwise, Bob wins. For which \( n \) can Alice guarantee a win, regardless of the initial sequence \( a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n \)?

Consider a \(3 \times 3\) grid of points where each point is connected to its nearest neighbors by line segments, forming a series of squares. A "worm" is defined as a closed polygonal chain that visits each point exactly once and returns to its starting point. Furthermore, this "worm" must form a sequence of right turns and left turns in such a way that the total number of right turns is exactly one more than the total number of left turns. How many distinct worms exist on this grid, up to rotation and reflection?

In a bag, there are 2019 marbles, each either red or blue. Suppose we add a red marble to the bag, and the number of possible distinct ordered pairs \((R, B)\) of red and blue marbles, respectively, increases by 46. Find the minimum number of blue marbles originally in the bag.

A group of \( n \) mathematicians are attending a conference. Each mathematician wears a unique, distinct hat labeled from 1 to \( n \). After the conference, they are assigned random hats. What is the probability that exactly \( k \) mathematicians end up with their own hats? Express your answer as a function of \( n \) and \( k \).

Alice and Bob are playing a game with a 5x5 grid of numbers. Each number is either 0, 1, or 2. They take turns choosing a 2x2 subgrid, and the player who chooses the subgrid must replace all numbers in that subgrid with the number that appears most frequently in that subgrid.
